result.rationale: The 2025 buyout closed and remains active, but Pike provides engineering, construction, maintenance and storm-response services for third-party infrastructure owners. TPG discussed Pike within Private Equity, La Caisse reports it under Private Equity, and no Pike-specific evidence ties it to Transition Infrastructure or proves qualifying utility/network ownership.

identityResolution.company: Pike Corporation, Mount Airy, North Carolina; founded 1945
identityResolution.falseMatch: ArcLight's Pike Holdings/Pike Petroleum/TLP entities belong to TransMontaigne and are unrelated.
identityResolution.boundary: Pike operating companies are subsidiaries, not separate sponsor PortCos.

ownershipResolution.security: Private-company equity; classes and percentages undisclosed.

owners.vehicle: Pilot Parent Holdings LP (Pike Corporation); Pilot Parent Holdings GP LLC also disclosed

owners.organization: J. Eric Pike, James R. Wyche and continuing investors

ownershipResolution.strategyFinding: Exact TPG fund/SPV is undisclosed. TPG and La Caisse classify Pike with Private Equity; neither attributes it to Transition Infrastructure.

operatingResolution.businessModel: Engineering, construction, maintenance, storm restoration and project delivery for utility, telecom and renewable customers.
operatingResolution.assetOwnership: No reviewed source shows Pike owns the underlying regulated utilities, power/telecom networks or generation assets; it builds and services customers' assets.

acquisitionExitCheck.result: Announced 2025-11-17 and closed 2025-12-19. No later transfer, exit, restructuring or signed pending ownership deal was found; Pike still identifies TPG as majority owner.

milestones.event: TPG Rise Climate majority, La Caisse significant minority and management co-investment announced.
Lindsay Goldberg completed its sale; new ownership closed.
